# Harnesses

Agent harnesses and orchestration runtimes: tool-use loops, model–tool boundary controllers, decision/context reuse, harness self-improvement, and the token/cost efficiency of agent scaffolding.

| How Much Do Coding Agents Over-Edit, and Why? An Empirical Study of Unneeded Edits in Repository-Level Agent Patches | ★★★★☆ | [2611.34875](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34875) | Aakash Goel et al. | 2026-11-25 | 2026-11-26 | Delta Residue Attribution (DRA) replays agent trajectories, reverts each patch unit and reruns the task tests to measure whether edits are needed. On 7,660 resolved GitHub Copilot CLI trajectories from 18 frontier models, agents' code is on average at least as necessary as developers' (0.887 vs 0.864 on SWE-bench Verified, 11 of 18 models leaving less unneeded code); most extra edits are tests (61%) and documentation (13%). Still, 11% of an agent patch's code units are unneeded and 89% of those change behavior; pruning with only the tests the agent can see removes most unneeded code, with 89% of pruned patches still resolving. |

| Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance | ★★★★☆ | [2611.33098](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33098) | Lingwei Gu, Jimmy Lin | 2026-11-24 | 2026-11-25 | A Claude Code-based agent harness in which the frontier model leads every task but delegates focused subtasks (code investigation, running tests, corpus search) to small-language-model subagents running on hardware you own. No router or model is trained, so either model can be swapped freely. With a 27B FP8 SLM it cuts frontier cost of long-horizon coding by 67% and agentic search by 59% with no loss in task performance; even a 2B SLM that fits on a laptop cuts coding cost by 66%. |
| Recursive Collective Intelligence: Emergence on an Equal-Budget Ladder in Multi-Agent LLM Systems | ★★★★☆ | [2611.32606](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32606) | Lixuan He et al. | 2026-11-24 | 2026-11-27 | Proposes the equal-budget ladder for grading multi-agent LLM teams against independent agents at the same token cost: beat one agent, beat a compute-matched majority vote, beat compute-matched pass@n. On six shared-question benchmarks (FATE-M, SWE-bench V, MMLongBench, LongBench v2, BrowseComp+, GPQA-D), existing methods (debate, DeLM, AOrchestra) fail to beat the same-cost vote — a plain vote over independent answers explains most reported multi-agent gains. Interaction helps when it moves information: with split facts, four 27B agents forwarding their facts reach 0.959 accuracy on HiddenBench, above an equal-budget full-information agent at 0.942. Identical 27B agents also spontaneously form hubs and improve accuracy by 18 points, and label-free recursive generations climb the ladder for four to six generations. Advice: check a same-cost vote before adding agents, and share raw facts rather than conclusions. |

### Context engineering & memory management

Context engineering, memory construction, and management.

| Paper | Importance | arXiv | Authors | Published | Added | Summary |

| Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought | ★★★★☆ | [2610.30755](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30755) | Zhengye Bao et al. | 2026-10-22 | 2026-11-27 | Raw-RAG, a naive RAG baseline (dense retrieval + reranking over raw chat history, 256-token chunks, flat vector index), ranks first among compared memory systems in six of seven benchmark-model settings across LoCoMo, LongMemEval, MEME and MemoryAgentBench, beating the strongest agentic memory system by 0.13-5.53 points. Higher coverage of necessary evidence offsets lower utilization, and even complete access to transformed memory stores leaves an accuracy gap vs raw evidence. Also far cheaper: ingesting a ~1M-token conversation takes 0.33h vs 26.95h for Memora; Mem0's effective mutations are only 1.90%/1.34% of write decisions, and append-only Mem0 lifts LoCoMo 67.36% to 69.42%. Challenges the necessity of complex agentic memory for conversation tasks; naive RAG is the essential baseline. |
